headline: US equity futures point lower as Gulf tensions lift oil over 2% ahead of jobless claims and busy earnings slate
raw_text:
- S&P 500 Futures (@ES) are down 1.01%, Dow Jones Futures (@YM) fall 0.62%, Nasdaq 100 Futures (@NQ) decline 1.76%, and Russell 2000 Futures (@ER2) drop 0.91%.
- Escalating geopolitical risks in the Gulf, including Houthi attacks, US diplomatic evacuations from Saudi Arabia, and reported strike planning on Iran, weigh on risk assets and push oil (@CL) prices up over 2%.
- Asian shares retreat overnight with the Kospi and Nikkei (@NKD) each down more than 2% and broader regional indexes weaker on combined tech/AI spending concerns and energy supply worries.
- European equity futures also point lower, mirroring weakness in US and Asian markets amid Mideast tensions and higher energy prices.
- Tesla (TSLA) slides about 5% pre-market as Bloomberg reports Elon Musk is pushing a Tesla–SpaceX merger targeted for early 2027, with the company also beating EPS estimates, missing on revenue, and cutting its 2026 capex outlook.
- Meta (META) trades slightly lower pre-market after an SEC filing details a Founder Alignment pact stapling 80% of Zuckerberg’s new Class C shares with an eight-year lockup, following mixed results that beat on revenue.
- Procter & Gamble (PG), Union Pacific (UNP), Lockheed Martin (LMT), Valero Energy (VLO), Spotify (SPOT), and Blackstone (BX) are scheduled to report earnings before the market open.
- Initial jobless claims are due at 8:30 AM ET and represent the main scheduled US economic data release for the session.
